title: Underived dg pullback pushforward adjunction on Hom complexes
statement:
Let $f:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ be a morphism of ringed topological spaces, meaning a continuous map with a unital ring-sheaf map $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Z\to\mathcal O_X$. Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal B$ be sheaf dg algebras over $\mathcal O_Z$ and $\mathcal O_X$, and let $\varphi:f^{-1}\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$ be a dg algebra map over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Z\to\mathcal O_X$. Use left sheaf dg modules and homogeneous signed maps as in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Put $F(N)=\mathcal B\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal C} f^{-1}N$, with direct-sum total tensor differential, and give the degreewise direct image $G(M)=f_*M$ its $\mathcal C$-action through the adjoint of $\varphi$. There is a natural isomorphism of complexes of abelian groups
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}^{\bullet}(F(N),M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}^{\bullet}(N,G(M)),$$
where Hom denotes global homogeneous sheaf maps and $\delta(h)=d h-(-1)^{|h|}h d$. In degree $r$, the isomorphism sends $h$ to the map adjoint to $n\mapsto h(1\otimes n)$; its inverse extends an adjoint $\widetilde k:f^{-1}N\to M$ by $b\otimes n\mapsto(-1)^{r|b|}b\widetilde k(n)$. The degree-zero closed maps give an adjunction $F\dashv G$ on dg modules and on their homotopy categories, with unit adjoint to $n\mapsto1\otimes n$ and counit induced by $b\otimes m\mapsto b\,\mathrm{ev}(m)$. Both functors preserve signed shifts and mapping cones. If $\mathcal B=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Z}f^{-1}\mathcal C$, there is a natural chain isomorphism $F(N)\cong\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Z}f^{-1}N$, induced by $(a\otimes c)\otimes n\mapsto a\otimes cn$ with inverse $a\otimes n\mapsto(a\otimes1)\otimes n$. Under this isomorphism the unit and counit have exactly their ordinary module-sheaf pullback/pushforward formulas after forgetting the action. For $f=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $\mathcal C=\mathcal O_X$ in degree zero, this is the free/forgetful Hom-complex adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}^{\bullet}(\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}L,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}^{\bullet}(L,UI)$. No exactness, flatness or boundedness assumption is made.

source.place: Tag 0FRU (lemma-adjunction-push-pull-dg), its graded predecessor lemma-adjunction-push-pull-gr, and section-functoriality-dg. Explicit left-module signed formulas and the base-change tensor identification unpack these constructions.

proof.text: Put $R=f^{-1}\mathcal O_Z$ and $A=f^{-1}\mathcal C$. Work on the sites of opens, with open covers, in the universes of the module definition. Preimage of opens carries a cover to a cover, so it is continuous. The set inverse image preserves finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-colimits-finite-products]. Thus [lem-sfb-site-inverse-image-multimap-universal] applies to every finite family of homogeneous components. It transports multiplication and module actions: define the transported operation by its value on tuples of unit images; associativity, the unit equation and the Leibniz equation hold because the two sides agree on those tuples, hence agree by uniqueness. This constructs $A$ and $f^{-1}N$ with their claimed dg structures. The ordinary module adjunction [lem-pc-module-inverse-image-adjunction], applied over $\mathcal O_Z$ in each pair of degrees, transposes $R$-linear maps $f^{-1}N^i\to M^{i+r}$ to $\mathcal O_Z$-linear maps $N^i\to f_*M^{i+r}$. Here $M$ is restricted along $R\to\mathcal O_X$. Direct image has the sectionwise action through $\mathcal C\to f_*\mathcal B$; its Leibniz equation is the equation in $M$ evaluated on inverse images of opens.

source.place: Tags 0FR7, 0FRT: construction of pull and push; sheaves.tex Tag 008Y

proof.text: First perform extension of scalars on $X$, without the inverse-image adjunction. For a signed $\mathcal B$-linear homogeneous map $h:\mathcal B\otimes_A f^{-1}N\to M$ of degree $r$, set $t(n)=h(1\otimes n)$. For homogeneous $c\in A^q$, balancing and signed linearity give $t(cn)=h(\varphi(c)\otimes n)=(-1)^{rq}\varphi(c)t(n)$. Conversely such an $R$-linear $t$ defines $h(b\otimes n)=(-1)^{r p}b\,t(n)$ for $b\in\mathcal B^p$. Indeed the two representatives of the balancing relation have images $(-1)^{r(p+q)}b\varphi(c)t(n)$ and $(-1)^{rp}b\,t(cn)$, which coincide. The formula is additive in each input, $R$-balanced, and $\mathcal O_X$-linear after multiplication by the first factor; it is signed $\mathcal B$-linear since replacing $b$ by $ab$ adds $r|a|$ to the exponent. The tensor universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal], the direct-sum and balanced-quotient construction in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization], and the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] extend these formulas uniquely to sheaf maps. Evaluation at $1$ and extension are inverse, since $h(b\otimes n)=(-1)^{rp}b\,h(1\otimes n)$. This also explains why checking formulas on homogeneous tensor generators suffices below; it never asserts that all global sections are pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 0FR8, lemma-adjunction-push-pull-gr: extension/restriction part of its hints, with explicit left-module signs

proof.text:
Transpose $t$ degreewise by step 1 to $k:N\to f_*M$. The signed $\mathcal C$-linearity of $k$ is equivalent to signed $A$-linearity of $t$. In fact, for $c\in\mathcal C^q(V)$ and $n\in N^i(V)$, the unit and action formulas give
$k(cn)=t(\eta(cn))=t(\eta(c)\eta(n))$ and $c\,k(n)=\varphi(\eta(c))t(\eta(n))$.
Thus signed linearity of $t$ implies that of $k$. Conversely, if $k$ is signed linear, the natural two-input maps $(a,x)\mapsto t(ax)$ and $(a,x)\mapsto(-1)^{rq}\varphi(a)t(x)$, from $A^q\times f^{-1}N^i$ to $M^{q+i+r}$, agree on all pairs of unit images. Uniqueness in [lem-sfb-site-inverse-image-multimap-universal] makes them equal everywhere. Together with step 2 this is an additive bijection in every degree, with precisely the forward and inverse formulas in the statement. Naturality in degree-zero module maps follows by substituting precomposition and postcomposition into these formulas and the natural module adjunction.

source.place: Tag 0FR8, lemma-adjunction-push-pull-gr: inverse-image/direct-image part of its hints

proof.text:
The signed homogeneous maps form Hom complexes: expanding the Leibniz rules gives $(\delta h)(am)=(-1)^{(r+1)|a|}a(\delta h)(m)$; the two terms involving $d(a)h(m)$ cancel. Expanding once more gives $\delta^2h=d^2h-hd^2=0$. Since $d(1)=0$, the tensor differential gives $d(1\otimes n)=1\otimes d(n)$, and hence
$(\delta h)(1\otimes n)=d_Mt(n)-(-1)^r t(dn)$.
The degreewise transpose commutes with differentials by naturality of the ordinary module adjunction. Therefore the additive bijections of step 3 commute with $\delta$; their inverses do also. This proves the asserted natural chain isomorphism, without exchanging any infinite sum with $f_*$.

source.place: Tag 0FRU, lemma-adjunction-push-pull-dg: the omitted differential calculation, using the Hom convention of Tag 0FRL
Tag 0FRT, section-functoriality-dg, enhancement to dg categories

proof.text: Restrict the chain isomorphism to degree-zero cycles; these are exactly the dg module morphisms. The identity of $F(N)$ transposes to the unit, namely the adjoint of $n\mapsto1\otimes n$. The inverse transpose of the identity of $G(M)$ is the counit $b\otimes m\mapsto b\,\mathrm{ev}(m)$, where $\mathrm{ev}:f^{-1}f_*M\to M$ is the ordinary inverse-image counit. The triangle identities can be checked explicitly: $F(N)\to FG F(N)\to F(N)$ sends $b\otimes n$ to $b\otimes\eta_N(n)$ and then to $b\otimes n$; $G(M)\to GF G(M)\to G(M)$ sends a section $m$ to $1\otimes m$ and then to $m$, using the inverse-image triangle identity. Tensor and sheafification uniqueness from step 2 give equality on all sections. These natural Hom bijections, unit and counit give $F\dashv G$.

source.place: Tag 0FRU, degree-zero cycles; sheaves.tex Tag 008K, ordinary adjunction unit and counit

proof.text: A module homotopy is a signed degree-$-1$ map $s$ with difference $\delta s=d s+s d$, exactly as in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Step 5 shows that both functors preserve this relation. Steps 3--4 send boundaries in degree zero bijectively to boundaries, so the Hom bijection descends to the quotients by homotopy and remains bijective and natural. The unit, counit and triangle identities descend as well. This proves the claimed adjunction of homotopy categories, with no appeal to a derived localization.

source.place: Tag 0FRZ, section-homotopy, applied to the explicit Hom chain isomorphism

proof.text: For any integer $k$, define $\theta_k:F(N[k])\to F(N)[k]$ by $b\otimes n\mapsto(-1)^{kp}b\otimes n$, $p=|b|$. In the source balancing relation the shifted action of $c\in A^q$ adds $kq$; the exponents $k(p+q)$ and $kp+kq$ coincide. For $a\in\mathcal B^q$, the target action adds $kq$, so $\theta_k(a(b\otimes n))=a\cdot_{F(N)[k]}\theta_k(b\otimes n)$. On $d(b)\otimes n$, the source-then-$\theta$ exponent is $k(p+1)$ and the $\theta$-then-target-differential exponent is $kp+k$; on $b\otimes dn$ both are $kp+p+k$. Thus $\theta_k$ is a chain map. Its inverse has the same sign, so it is an isomorphism. The signs add under consecutive shifts and the formula commutes with degree-zero maps. For $G$ the identity on each component gives $G(M[k])\cong G(M)[k]$, since the differential and action acquire exactly the same signs on both sides.

source.place: Tags 0FRC and 0FRY, signed shift convention translated to left modules

proof.text:
Let $u:N\to N'$ be a degree-zero chain map. Tensor distributes over the two summands of $C(u)=N'\oplus N[1]$: the forward map sends $b\otimes(n',n)$ to $(b\otimes n',b\otimes n)$, and its inverse is the sum of the two maps induced by the inclusions. These are inverse by bilinearity and the balanced tensor universal property from step 2. Composing on the second summand with $\theta_1$ of step 8 gives
$F(C(u))\longrightarrow C(Fu),\quad b\otimes(n',n)\longmapsto(b\otimes n',(-1)^p b\otimes n)$.
The diagonal differential terms commute by step 8. The off-diagonal term on the source is $(-1)^p b\otimes u(n)$; on the target it is $Fu((-1)^p b\otimes n)$, the same element. The inverse again has the same sign. This intertwines the cone inclusion and projection with the shift comparison, hence also the specified $-p$ triangle arrow. Direct image preserves the two summands since sections of a finite direct sum are the finite product of sections; it preserves the displayed differential matrix entrywise. It therefore gives $G(C(v))\cong C(Gv)$ with the identical inclusions and projections. Both functors preserve mapping cones with the stated signed conventions.

source.place: Tag 0FS5, definition-cone; Tag 0FRT and the explicit shift comparison

proof.text: Now suppose $\mathcal B=\mathcal O_X\otimes_R A$. Define $\alpha((a\otimes c)\otimes n)=a\otimes cn$ and $\beta(a\otimes n)=(a\otimes1)\otimes n$. The inner $R$-balancing moves a scalar between $a$ and $c$; the outer $A$-balancing moves $c$ to $n$. Both leave $a\otimes cn$ unchanged, so $\alpha$ is well defined; the same $R$-balancing proves that $\beta$ is. They define sheaf maps by the tensor and sheafification universal properties, including arbitrary direct-sum degrees. The two composites are identities: $\alpha\beta(a\otimes n)=a\otimes n$, while $\beta\alpha((a\otimes c)\otimes n)=(a\otimes1)\otimes cn=(a\otimes c)\otimes n$. For $|c|=q$, both differentials after $\alpha$ are $a\otimes(d(c)n+(-1)^q c\,dn)$; $a$ has degree zero and differential zero. The maps are natural in $N$ and linear for the transported $\mathcal B$-action. Hence this is the asserted chain isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0FRT, definition of pullback; base-change tensor identification by its balanced presentation

proof.text: Under $\alpha$, the unit of step 6 sends $n$ to $1\otimes n$, and the counit sends $a\otimes m$ to $a\,\mathrm{ev}(m)$. These are exactly ordinary module-sheaf pullback and pushforward formulas after forgetting the action. Finally take $f=\mathrm{id}$ and $\mathcal C=\mathcal O_X$ in degree zero: inverse image and its adjunction are identities, $F(L)=\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}L$ and $G(I)=UI$. The formula of steps 2--4 becomes the asserted free/forgetful Hom-complex adjunction. Every argument used direct-sum tensor constructions, finite products or Hom groups, never preservation of exact sequences, so no flatness, exactness or boundedness is required.
